title: In zsh a command stored in a variable is one word and fails with 'no such file'

keywords: no such file or directory: python3

symptom: L="python3 …/launch_cli.py"; $L web … fails with 'no such file or directory: python3 /…/launch_cli.py'
cause: zsh does not split variables into words (unlike bash)
fix: Call the fixed entry point directly: python3 ~/.projectops/bin/launch_cli.py doctor
To repeat it, wrap it in a function: launch() { python3 "$HOME/.projectops/bin/launch_cli.py" "$@"; }
Do not store several arguments in one variable like 'web $a' (use bash -c if needed)
